Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao is a flagship

initiative under Mission Shakti aimed at

addressing issues of declining child sex ratio and

ensuring survival, protection and empowerment of

girl children. The key activities under this scheme

include training and capacity building

programmes, preparation and distribution of IEC

materials, skill development initiatives, higher

education and career guidance.

32

An amount of Rs.10.70 crore has been

allocated in the Revised Budget Estimate for the

1.2.3 Awards

i. Recognition of bravery of girl children

To recognize and encourage the

achievement of girl children and to acknowledge

the efforts in preventing child labour, child

marriage and other social evils against girl

children, a State Award for Girl Child

Empowerment is given to one girl child every year

in the form of a cash prize of Rs.1,00,000 and an

appreciation certificate.

ii. Recognition of Districts for increasing Child Sex Ratio

Tamil Nadu Girl Child Protection Day is

celebrated on 24th February. On this occasion,

the Government of Tamil Nadu recognises three

districts that have shown significant improvement

33

in child sex ratio. The Collectors of these districts

are presented with cash awards of Rs.1,00,000,

Rs.75,000 and Rs.50,000 and certificates of

appreciation.

1.2.4 Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme

Launched in 2022, the Chief Minister’s

Breakfast Scheme for school children is being

implemented in Tamil Nadu for students of class I

to V with the objectives of addressing

malnutrition, increasing school attendance/

retention, enabling better focus and attention in

the classrooms and decreasing the burden of

working mothers. To honour Perunthalaivar

Kamarajar for his pioneering initiative of providing

meals to children in school with a view of

promoting education, the Chief Minister’s

Breakfast Scheme has been named as

Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme.

34

The scheme covers 19.34 lakh students in

classes I to V, across 37,447 schools. In the

current year 2026-27, the scheme is being

expanded to cover 15,14,274 students studying in

classes VI to VIII in 15,454 Government and

Government-aided schools.

The scheme is implemented across the

State through two distinct operational models to

ensure efficient delivery of nutritious meals. In

urban areas, the scheme is implemented by the

Greater Chennai Corporation and the Municipal

Administration Department, with meals prepared

in centralized kitchens by women Self Help

Groups (SHGs) and vendors. In rural areas, the

implementation is carried out in kitchens located

within school premises by women SHGs through

the Tamil Nadu Corporation for Development of

of education and creating a conducive

atmosphere for teaching and learning. The

Directorate continues to strengthen school

infrastructure by augmenting classrooms,

laboratories, sanitation, drinking water and

compound wall facilities.

a) Manarkeni - Digital Learning Platform

Digital learning has become an integral

component of academic improvement.

Manarkeni, Tamil Nadu's State-owned digital

39

learning platform, provides curriculum-aligned

digital resources in both Tamil and English to

support classroom instruction, board examination

preparation, competitive examinations, remedial

learning and teacher professional development.

The platform currently serves over 30 lakh

users through an extensive repository comprising

13,000 learning videos, 2.5 lakh practice

questions and 5,800 study materials. By

enabling students and teachers to access quality

digital content anytime and anywhere, Manarkeni

has significantly strengthened blended learning

and digital pedagogy across Government schools.

To ensure effective implementation,

1.2.5 Puratchi Thalaivar MGR Nutritious Meal Programme

Tamil Nadu is the pioneer in school nutrition

initiatives, beginning with the introduction of a

school meal programme in the Chennai

Corporation (then Madras Corporation) in 1920.

In 1956, the programme was subsequently

expanded to primary schools across the State. In

1982, the programme evolved into the Nutritious

Meal Programme (NMP), one of the largest and

most enduring school feeding initiatives in the

country. Over the years, several nutritional

enhancements have been introduced, including

the provision of eggs to address protein

deficiencies and a variety of hot, freshly cooked

mixed rice meals.

Drawing insights from the success of the

Puratchi Thalaivar MGR Nutrious Meal Programme

in Tamil Nadu, the Government of India in 1998

launched National Programme of Nutritional

Support to Primary Education across the country,

37

which is now implemented as PM POSHAN for

classes I - VIII in the cost sharing pattern of

60:40 between Government of India and State

Governments.

Under the Puratchi Thalaivar MGR Nutritious

Meal Programme, delicious, hot and nutritious

mixed rice varieties along with masala eggs are

provided to students of class I to X in Government

and Government aided schools on all school

working days. The programme is implemented

through 42,984 centres, benefitting 39.27 lakh

students.

The programme is strengthened through

food fortification measures including the use of

double-fortified salt (iodine and iron) and fortified

cooking oil enriched with Vitamins A and D. The

nutritional standards under this scheme exceed

national norms, providing higher level of calories

and protein to primary, upper primary and high

38

school students. This contributes significantly to

improved health, growth and learning outcomes.

elementary education. The Directorate continues

to fill vacant posts through regular recruitment

16

temporary teachers through School Management

continuity in classroom instruction.

2.10 Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Morning

Breakfast Scheme

Food is being provided under the

Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme to all

students studying in Classes 1 to 5 across 37,447

Government and Government Aided schools. In

the current academic year, the scheme will be

extended to students in Classes 6 to 8. A total of

34,48,504 students studying in Classes 1 to 8 will

be benefitted from this scheme. An allocation of

Rs. 724.52 crore has been made for this initiative.

2.11 Conclusion

The Directorate of Elementary Education

continues to strengthen the foundations of school

education through sustained investments in

access, academic quality, teacher’s capacity and

institutional excellence. By integrating school

modernisation, teacher professional development

and learner-centred educational practices, the

Directorate is creating an enabling ecosystem

18

that supports better learning outcomes and

holistic child development. These initiatives

ensure that children complete elementary

education with strong foundational competencies

and are well prepared for the next stage of

schooling, contributing to Tamil Nadu's longterm

educational development.

19

CHAPTER III

Directorate of School Education

3.1 Introduction

The Directorate of School Education (DSE)

is responsible for planning, administering and

strengthening school education for students

studying in Classes VI to XII in Tamil Nadu. It

plays a pivotal role in improving the quality of

teaching and learning, promoting academic

excellence, ensuring equitable and inclusive

access to secondary and higher secondary

education and implementing student support

programmes. Through a range of academic,

vocational, co-curricular and student development

initiatives, the Directorate prepares students for

higher education, employment and responsible

citizenship.

20

11.5. Educational Scholarship

The Government provides educational

scholarship every year to encourage school

attendance among differently abled students and

to promote their Special Education. The

scholarship amount is sanctioned according to

the class of the student.

This initiative helps to prevent school

dropouts among differently abled students,

facilitate their continued education and create

opportunities for them to pursue higher

education.

11.6. Cash Incentive Scheme to Prevent School Dropout

Differently abled students are encouraged

to pursue higher education and to prevent them

from discontinuing their studies, an annual

incentive ranging from ₹1,500/- to ₹2,000/- is

provided to students studying in Classes X, XI

and XII.

Under this scheme, the incentive

amount is deposited as a fixed investment in the

Tamil Nadu Power Finance and Infrastructure

Development Corporation Limited (TNPFC) in the

interest of the students' future welfare. Upon the

successful completion of Class XII, the

accumulated incentive amount, together with

the applicable interest, is credited directly to the

student's bank account. The details of cash
